facts.text: Cypress Hills Cemetery opened in 1851 as New York City’s first non‑sectarian cemetery, a response to 19th‑century public health concerns.
In 1862 a northwest section became Cypress Hills National Cemetery, burying 3,425 Union soldiers and 478 Confederates from the Civil War.
The 1983 founding of the Cypress Hills Local Development Corporation turned a struggling neighborhood into a national model for community‑led revitalization.
German, Irish, and Italian immigrants settled Cypress Hills in the late 1800s, drawn by cheap lots and nearby factory jobs.
Before railroads, the area was rural farmland owned by Dutch and English families, later transformed by the Long Island Rail Road’s Great Eastern line.
In 1998 a scandal revealed part of the cemetery was built on unstable landfill, leading to a Supreme Court ruling that graves had to be moved.
